attacks.claim: Cost arithmetic is wrong by ~30x. 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens per DAY; at $0.50/M that is ~$1,140/day, roughly $34k/month, over 20x the $1,500 budget. Output line has the same daily-vs-monthly error. Peak days (61M) and the repeated prompt overhead make it worse. The core design (send every line) is not viable within budget.
attacks.evidence: Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140 ... Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget.

attacks.claim: Staffing assumes both engineers 100% for 6 weeks, but the context states on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time. Effective capacity is ~6 eng-weeks against 12 planned, with no contingency, so the schedule is not credible.
attacks.evidence: Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks).

attacks.claim: No spend cap, sampling, truncation, or circuit breaker is defined. Error storms during incidents and peak days spike volume and cost exactly when the tool is needed, with no behaviour when the budget is exhausted.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any per-day/monthly token budget, hard spend limit on the Corvid account, or behaviour when the budget is exhausted.

attacks.claim: Privacy rests on a redaction stage that masks only emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs. Names, free-text user input, and customer identifiers are not covered. Every log line goes to a third-party LLM, and the plan does not verify redaction coverage against this data flow or that the DPA covers it.
attacks.evidence: which already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)

attacks.claim: log-tap sits on the production Vector pipeline with no stated backpressure isolation, so a full summarizer queue could slow or drop the logs needed for investigation. There is also no kill switch or rollback for the tap or the PagerDuty comments.
attacks.evidence: log-tap (new): subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline after the redaction stage and forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue.

attacks.claim: Failure modes are unaddressed: LLM outage, timeouts, rate limits (30 services hitting the same 5-minute boundary with ~264k+ tokens per call), malformed output, and stale or missing summaries in the PagerDuty comment. Responders may act on a stale summary without knowing.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout/retry policy, fallback when summarizer is down, staleness marking on the PagerDuty comment, and alerting on summarizer health.

attacks.claim: The 'suspected deploy' field has no defined data source; no deploy-event integration is listed.
attacks.evidence: stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy).

attacks.claim: The evaluation is weak: the same 40 incidents are used for prompt development and grading (no held-out split), with a single grader. The 47→30 min MTTR target has no measurement plan or mechanism.
The 5-minute window cadence conflicts with 'within seconds of a page'; the summary attached at page time may be stale and miss the onset of the failure.
attacks.evidence: every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service

attacks.claim: There is no output sanitisation against prompt injection from log content, no source citations back to log lines, and no retention policy for stored summaries.
